angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 468,902 km at 58.68 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.0430 +/- 0.0096 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 58.68 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.674 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Vach et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-712 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...71V/abstract): 468,902 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.732 +/- 0.027 solar masses from Vach et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-712 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...71V/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4622 +/- 61 K from Vach et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-712 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...71V/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Vach et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-712 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...71V/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-712.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.645, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
